chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, from 'Ali, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a mouse that falls into the well. He said: seven buckets. He said: And I asked him about a bird and a chicken that fall into the well. He said: seven buckets.

key_terms.الدَّجَاجَةِ: a chicken; included in the same ruling
key_terms.الطَّيْرِ: a bird; included in the ruling regarding the well
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is under discussion for purification
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse; here, an animal falling into the well
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets; the prescribed amount of water to be drawn out

ai.seo_question: How many buckets should be drawn from a well if a mouse, bird, or chicken falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity when a mouse, bird, or chicken falls into a well. The Imam عليه السلام states that seven buckets of water are to be drawn from the well in such cases, indicating a practical fiqh ruling for purification.
